summary: The camera scanner returns the raw decoded barcode string (e.g., 12-digit UPC-A or 13-digit EAN-13) and passes it directly to the exact GTIN lookup without normalizing it to the canonical GTIN-14 representation. The decoder only validates that the text can be normalized (via Gtin.normalize) but does not return the normalized value.
claim: If the exact GTIN lookup expects zero-padded 14-digit GTIN values, scanning a valid UPC-A (12 digits) or EAN-13 (13 digits) may return no candidates, violating the owner requirement that a scan must populate the existing exact GTIN lookup.

evidence.source: In BarcodeCamera.kt, decodeGtin returns `reader.decodeWithState(...).text.takeIf { Gtin.normalize(it) != null }`, which is the raw text. In MainActivity.kt, the onBarcode callback sets `model.query = code; model.search()` with that raw text. The provided code does not call Gtin.normalize on the result before passing it to the lookup.

suggested_remediation: Normalize the decoded GTIN to the canonical 14-digit form before assigning it to model.query, or ensure that model.search performs identical normalization internally and document that behavior.
suggested_validation: Scan a known UPC-A barcode present in the catalog and verify the correct candidate appears; repeat for an EAN-13 barcode.
